topics.title: Getting Started
topics.summary: Start with a text-only conversation, then add speech and an avatar.
bullets: Run INSTALL_NEURAL_COMPANION.bat, then launch run_neural_companion.bat.
In Runtime → Runtime Session → LLM, configure the provider and model, test the connection, then choose Make active.
In Session setup choose Text Only. Activate None for Text-to-speech and Avatar for a silent first test.
Use Initialize NC in the header, wait for readiness, then send a greeting in Conversation → Main chat.
Addons → Tutorials → First Run and docs/manual/first-run.md explain the setup.

topics.title: Navigation and Hidden Controls
topics.summary: The native desktop has Runtime, Addons, Conversation, Visual Reply, and Avatar Preview views.
bullets: Runtime contains Runtime Session, Vision Sensors, Chat Behavior, Story Visuals, Document Memory, and Appearance Themes.
Provider settings are inside Runtime Session. Viewing settings does not activate a provider.
Use the NeuralCompanion logo/name menu to restore hidden workspaces, and Unhide addon to restore hidden addon icons.
Conversation Controls manages which chat actions are visible. Workspaces can also be docked or floated.

topics.title: Language Providers
topics.summary: Configure the connection and select an active provider in Runtime → Runtime Session → LLM.
bullets: LM Studio and Ollama need a running server and an available model. Check the base URL, refresh the models, and test the connection.
Hosted providers need API credentials and a model your account can access.
Choose Make active; merely opening a provider's settings does not switch normal chat.
A saved Persona override can select another provider/model. Check its effective settings if normal Runtime settings do not explain a reply.

topics.title: Speech Output and Streaming
topics.summary: Select and activate speech output separately from the language model and microphone.
bullets: Open Runtime → Runtime Session → Text-to-speech, configure a provider and choose Use for voice output.
None intentionally gives silent text replies. Check the header Audio menu for the output device and level.
Assign a compatible voice in Persona. Previewing a sample does not assign it.
Streaming splits speech into chunks; latency and expressive tags depend on the selected backend and settings.
In rooms the full reply can appear before its audio is ready; speech highlighting tracks playback separately.

topics.title: Microphone Input
topics.summary: Microphone transcription depends on the session input mode and active speech-to-text provider.
bullets: Choose the input mode in Runtime → Runtime Session → Session setup. Text Only disables microphone transcription.
Configure and activate a provider in Speech-to-text with Use for speech input.
Select the input device in the header Audio menu and check Windows microphone permissions.
For Push-to-Talk, check your configured binding in Addons → Hotkeys.
Discord mode receives voice from Discord, with separate incoming-voice and room-routing controls.

topics.title: PocketTTS
topics.summary: PocketTTS providers use a separate local speech runtime.
bullets: Install the PocketTTS target with the NC installer, then configure it under Runtime → Runtime Session → Text-to-speech.
Cloning can require accepting model terms and logging in to Hugging Face inside the isolated PocketTTS environment.
Check model access and the voice reference before changing generation settings.
See docs/manual/pockettts.md for setup and troubleshooting.

topics.title: Personas and Overrides
topics.summary: Persona stores a character's prompt, voice, portraits, and optional reply-setting overrides.
bullets: Open Addons → Persona and save the character you want to use.
Voice, visual identity, and language-model settings are separate choices.
Persona Overrides can change the provider/model, conversation context limit, and Document Memory behavior.
An unavailable override provider/model reports an error; it does not silently select another model.
Switching personas in main chat does not create a new conversation history.

topics.title: User Identity
topics.summary: User Identity describes you for supported main-chat and image workflows.
bullets: Open the User Identity addon to edit the local user profile and optional portrait.
Discord human participants use their Discord identity. A local User Identity change does not rename your Discord account.
Use Discord's own profile/server nickname controls to change your Discord display name.
In a Discord room the sender chooser distinguishes a connected human from NC operator input.

topics.title: Conversation and Document Memory
topics.summary: Saved-chat memory and Document Memory are different features.
bullets: Save or load a named main chat before using its conversation summary and older-message memory controls.
Keeping summaries or storing messages and allowing them to influence replies are separate controls.
Runtime → Document Memory manages document packages and recall. Select a package, check indexing, and test search before enabling it in chat.
Imported document snapshots do not follow edits to original files automatically; use Refresh from sources.
See docs/manual/memory.md for settings, persona overrides, and data handling.

topics.title: Avatar Engines
topics.summary: Choose an avatar provider under Runtime → Runtime Session → Avatar.
bullets: MuseTalk and Ditto need their own runtime, models, and prepared engine-specific assets.
Scenic uses expression images; VSeeFace uses an external application and configured receiver.
Choose Use this avatar to activate the selected route. Opening Avatar Preview alone does not start a model.
None disables animated-avatar rendering and works with silent or spoken chat.
See docs/manual/avatars.md for engine-specific setup.

topics.title: MuseTalk Preparation and Performance
topics.summary: Prepare an avatar asset separately from selecting it for conversation playback.
bullets: Use the MuseTalk or Ditto creator appropriate to the target engine; their packages are not interchangeable.
Select the prepared asset in the corresponding Runtime Avatar provider and activate it.
MuseTalk performance and supported emotion variants depend on the runtime configuration and prepared pack.
Older Body, Dynamics, and Hand Doctor instructions describe earlier interfaces; use the current provider and creator guides.
See docs/manual/musetalk.md, docs/manual/ditto.md, and docs/avatar_packs.md.

topics.title: Performance and Chunking
topics.summary: Measure the active model, speech, and avatar stack before adjusting performance.
bullets: Use the available Dry Run and Performance controls for bounded timing checks and saved performance profiles.
A first reply can include downloads, model loading, and cold caches; compare later replies too.
Smaller speech chunks can begin earlier but may make phrasing less natural; change one setting at a time.
Performance profiles and Persona settings have different purposes.
See docs/manual/performance.md for the controls available in your build.

topics.title: Expressive Tags
topics.summary: Expression and vocal tags are interpreted by the selected speech/avatar providers.
bullets: Prepared avatar variants determine which visual emotions can be shown.
Supported vocal tags and the resulting sounds differ between speech backends.
A text tag is not a guarantee that every provider will render the same action.
Use short examples with your active voice and avatar before relying on a tag in a longer conversation.

topics.title: Visual Reply
topics.summary: Visual Reply generates images using the configured image provider.
bullets: Configure and activate the provider in Runtime → Runtime Session → Visual reply.
ComfyUI is a separate local or LAN server and needs the workflow's models and nodes installed.
The Visual Reply workspace browses images; provider configuration and image display are separate.
Persona visual-identity references and appearance settings affect eligible generated images.
See docs/manual/visual-reply-and-sensory.md and docs/visual_reply_toolbar.md.

topics.title: Vision Sensors and Companion Orb
topics.summary: Observation and proactive reactions require their own source and awareness controls.
bullets: Configure sources and permissions in Runtime → Vision Sensors.
Showing the Companion Orb does not automatically start a watch or capture your desktop.
Choose the target and review which background reactions are enabled.
Captured context is sent through the model routes you configure, including hosted providers when selected.

topics.title: AI Presence
topics.summary: AI Presence provides audio-reactive floating or fullscreen visuals.
bullets: Open the AI Presence addon and choose the visual mode and audio-sync settings.
Desktop audio sync analyzes the default playback output. Confirm sound is playing on that device.
Check sensitivity and noise gate if the visual does not react.
The Living Voice Thread preset controls load, save, and restore its tuning. Presets are distinct from Persona or performance profiles.

topics.title: Local and Discord Rooms
topics.summary: Rooms run moderated discussions with linked Personas and their own saved conversation state.
bullets: Open Addons → Discord Voice → Local room and choose Local or Discord mode.
Configure participants and their effective providers/voices before starting.
You can change participants during a conversation; current speech finishes before a removal is applied.
Participants retain what they heard while present; returning does not give them speech delivered while absent.
Follow stop/save prompts when switching between main chat and a room.

topics.title: Discord Bot Accounts
topics.summary: Reusable Discord bot accounts are assigned to Personas in the room.
bullets: Add accounts in the Discord tab's Bot accounts section. Saving checks a token; Check all accounts refreshes account verification.
Checking an account is separate from inviting it to a server or connecting to voice.
Choose a prepared account on the Persona's room card. A running/reserved account may not be free for another participant.
The server nickname follows the assigned Persona; it does not rename the Discord account globally.
See docs/addons/discord_voice.md for setup and permissions.

topics.title: Discord Incoming Voice and Sender
topics.summary: Discord admission, NC incoming-voice acceptance, and room routing are separate controls.
bullets: Discord determines who can join a channel.
Everyone ignores the optional user-ID list. Listed users uses it; an empty list accepts everyone's incoming voice.
Separate IDs with commas, spaces, or semicolons. Save settings and restart the bridge to apply voice-filter changes.
Room speaker controls and protected-speech settings determine whether accepted speech is routed during a reply.
Typed room input enters NC's conversation. Choose a connected human or NC operator; it is not a Discord user-account text post.

topics.title: Buddy Chat
topics.summary: Buddy Chat adds several companions to main chat using a staged setup preview.
bullets: Choose the refinement scope and the intended Persona/field, then give a specific instruction.
Refine with LLM updates valid editable fields in the staged preview, not an unrelated saved Persona automatically.
Read Current status for completion or validation feedback, inspect the preview, and apply the staged setup when ready.
See docs/addons/buddy_chat.md for setup, voice assignment, and refinement controls.

topics.title: Stories and Roleplay
topics.summary: Audio Story Mode and Multi Persona Roleplay have their own project and playback workflows.
bullets: Roleplay builds a cast and scenes, with a separate Play view.
Audio Story Mode organizes chapters, transcripts, planning, illustrations, and narration.
Configure the required model, speech, and optional image services before a long production run.
Start with a short scene or chapter and read the relevant addon guide.

topics.title: Phone and Internet Remote
topics.summary: Main Chat Remote connects a compatible phone client to the desktop's main conversation.
bullets: Keep the desktop and required runtime running; the phone does not run the desktop models.
Use LAN pairing locally, or configure Internet mode with NC Relay and a matching native phone build.
Internet signaling and the selected WebRTC media route are different: media can be direct or relayed depending on the connection.
Check diagnostics for the selected route rather than assuming that Internet mode always uses TURN.
See docs/addons/main_chat_remote.md and docs/addons/main_chat_remote_internet_setup.md.

topics.title: Addons and Tutorials
topics.summary: Addons provide tools, experiences, and provider choices; Tutorials explains the current interface.
bullets: Find addon workspaces under Addons; provider addons also appear in their Runtime role.
Use Addon Manager for enabled state and follow any after-restart notice.
A hidden icon is different from a disabled addon; use Unhide addon when appropriate.
Start with Tutorials → First Run, or use the written manual and addon catalog under docs/.

topics.title: Presets and Saved State
topics.summary: Persona presets, performance profiles, addon presets, and saved conversations have different scopes.
bullets: A Persona preset does not select every machine-specific runtime/provider option.
Save conversations separately when you want to reopen their transcript.
AI Presence and other tools can have their own preset selectors; check which tool's Save action you are using.
Session settings and logs can contain credentials or private data. Do not publish them.

topics.title: Limitations and Troubleshooting
topics.summary: Test a small working configuration and diagnose the failing component before changing the whole setup.
bullets: Read readiness/status messages and the Conversation console.
Test an active chat provider with Text Only input, None speech, and None avatar.
Optional runtimes, models, assets, external servers, and API credentials are separate prerequisites.
Windows and Python 3.11 are the expected desktop baseline; hardware and service availability affect optional features.
See docs/troubleshooting.md and docs/known_limitations.md.
